state:
Milestone `dossier`, goal `the-description-is-owed`, stage 2. `data/proofs/policy.json` carries
`owes.all.about: true`, and every feature whose examples were on disk when this goal first ran has
its description: the 13 sections of `tools:config` were the last, and
`bun nv proofs --verify --group tools:config` passes.

**This goal now sits behind goals `tools-install` and `tools-server` on the chain.** Its one check,
`bun nv proofs --gate`, is the whole roster, and those two goals own the features it still named.
Each of them writes its features' descriptions with their other proofs, because the policy already
makes a description owed. So when the chain comes back here the check is expected to pass as the
tree stands, and a feature it still names is one a goal in front left behind.

**Two things for the user to look at.** `docs/reference/tools/20-config.md:65-70` says `nvs run`
enforces `[limits] memory` alone and that the server, database client and logger are not in the
binary. Line 165 of the same chapter says `memory` and `cpu_time`, a run under `cpu_time = "1s"`
stops with `FATAL: the request exceeded its CPU-time limit`, and `nvs --help` lists `serve`. The
paragraph was left as it stands, because rewriting it needs each block checked against `nvs run`,
and the new descriptions state none of it. Carried forward and not re-checked: gap
`nvs-ir/throws-on-an-array-key-that` was moved from owner goal `coalesce-assign` back to
`milestone: M10`, and `docs/agent/goals/coalesce-assign.md` still has that goal delete it.

The pack does not print `docs/examples/README.md` § *The description*; it is one `bun nv peek`.
A group is checked with `bun nv proofs --gate --group '<G>'`.
